title: High-efficiency and salt-resistant solar desalination using 3D-printed PLA/carbon fiber composite evaporators with arrayed axial–radial dual-transport
content: The performance of solar interfacial evaporation is intrinsically limited by the coupled heat and mass transfer resistance within the device and the associated crystallization fouling at the evaporation surface. Inspired by the axial–radial water transport in trees, we develop a biomimetic arrayed axial–radial dual-transport evaporator (AARDE) using 3D printing of PLA/carbon fiber composites. One-step FDM shaping followed by hot-water conditioning enables complex architectures with interconnected water transport pathways, enabling highly efficient and salt-resistant solar desalination. The composite evaporator achieves 96% broadband absorption (300–2500 nm), and excellent mechanical and thermal stability. Thermal characterization reveals that the 3D architecture significantly reduces the heat loss from the evaporation zone to the bulk water, maintaining a localized interfacial temperature elevation. In addition, an optimized arrayed grid topology could enhance side-surface evaporation. As a result, the system delivers evaporation rates of 3.55 kg m−2 h−1 in pure water and 3.10 kg m−2 h−1 in 10 wt% brine, with stable salt-free status on the main evaporation surface. Field testing demonstrates a daily freshwater production of 25 L m−2 under natural sunlight, as well as successful purification of seawater and dye-contaminated wastewater. This work highlights the unique advantage of 3D printing technology to fabricate intricate structures toward durable and salt-resistant solar evaporators for sustainable freshwater generation.
